analysis.title: O'Reilly Automotive Inc. (ORLY): First Take: 3Q26 top- and bottom-line beat; FY26 outlook raised
key_insights: ORLY reported 3Q26 EPS of $0.97 vs GS estimate $0.94 and consensus (FactSet) $0.93. Excluding a $39mn benefit from tariff refunds received in the quarter, EPS was $0.93, in line with consensus.
Sales rose 8.8% y/y to $5.121bn vs GS $5.023bn and consensus $5.018bn. Comparable-store sales rose 7.2% vs GS 4.0% and consensus 4.5%.

Operating margin expanded 70bps y/y to 21.4% vs GS 21.0% and consensus 20.8%. Gross margin rose 54bps and SG&A as a % of sales fell 16bps. Excluding tariff refunds, operating margin was 20.7% (-6bps y/y), a slight miss vs GS and consensus.

Excluding the tariff refund benefit, gross margin was 51.6% (-22bps y/y), a miss vs GS and consensus estimates. The reported gross margin of 52.4% (+54bps y/y) beat the GS estimate of 52.1% and consensus of 52.0%.

Management raised FY26 guidance: comparable-store sales +5.5% to +6.5% (from +4.0% to +6.0%), revenue $19.0bn-$19.3bn (from $18.9bn-$19.2bn), gross margin 51.6%-52.1% (from 51.5%-52.0%), operating margin 19.5%-20.0% (from 19.3%-19.8%), EPS $3.25-$3.35 (from $3.20-$3.30).
Free cash flow guidance was raised to $1.9bn-$2.2bn (from $1.8bn-$2.1bn). Cash from operations is $3.2bn-$3.6bn (from $3.1bn-$3.5bn). Capex is $1.3bn-$1.4bn, unchanged.
Two- and three-year stacked comps accelerated sequentially to +12.8% and +14.3%, from +10.1% and +12.4% in the prior quarter.
DIY sales rose 6.2% y/y to $2.448bn and DIFM sales rose 12.7% y/y to $2.601bn. Sales mix was roughly 48%/52% DIY/DIFM vs 50%/50% a year earlier.
The accounts payable to inventory ratio fell 408bps y/y to 121.8%, from 123.7% in the prior quarter and 125.9% a year earlier.
ORLY repurchased 11.8mn shares for $1.035bn in the quarter vs GS estimate of $1.000bn, plus a further $204mn after quarter end. Year-to-date repurchases total $3.672bn vs $2.097bn in FY25.
GS expects a positive reaction to the beat and raise. Topics for the call: quarter-to-date trends, DIY vs DIFM, DIFM pricing, supply chain, market share gains, and traffic vs ticket.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy and keeps ORLY on the US Conviction List after a 3Q26 beat and FY26 guidance raise. The $113 12-month target implies 24.9% upside from $90.44.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 EPS $0.97 reported vs GS est $0.94 and consensus (FactSet) est $0.93. Excluding the $39mn tariff refund benefit, EPS was $0.93, in line with consensus.
3Q26 sales $5.121bn reported (+8.8% y/y) vs GS est $5.023bn and consensus est $5.018bn. Comparable-store sales +7.2% reported vs GS est +4.0% and consensus est +4.5%.
3Q26 operating margin 21.4% reported (+70bps y/y) vs GS est 21.0% and consensus est 20.8%. Ex tariff refunds it was 20.7% (-6bps y/y).
3Q26 gross margin 52.4% reported (+54bps y/y) vs GS est 52.1% and consensus est 52.0%. Ex tariff refunds it was 51.6% (-22bps y/y).
3Q26 SG&A ratio 30.9% reported (-16bps y/y) vs GS est 31.0% and consensus est 31.2%.
FY26 guidance raised: EPS $3.25-$3.35 (from $3.20-$3.30), revenue $19.0bn-$19.3bn, comps +5.5% to +6.5%. GS FY26E EPS is $3.32.
3Q26 share count 812.2mn vs GS est 809.0mn. Net income $786mn vs GS est $763mn. Tax rate 23.1% vs GS est 22.5%.
risk_factors: Demand headwinds, particularly in discretionary categories, from broader macro pressure.
Elevated inflation in certain non-controllable expenses.
Higher distribution costs from supply chain headwinds and labor cost increases.
Operating margin risk as DIFM penetration rises and ORLY invests in recruiting and retaining talent.
Purchase deferral and other DIY demand headwinds.
Part of the reported gross and operating margin beat came from a one-time $39mn tariff refund benefit.
